about: KJV word helps: calm short glosses with optional deep-dive study fields. Hub concordance lists a growing subset of lemmas; each entry includes a concordance key for Search. See scripts/README-kjv-word-notes.md.

words.note: Often means self-giving love (caritas), not fundraising or a donation drive.
words.shortGloss: Often means self-giving love (caritas), not fundraising or a donation drive.
words.step: In 1 Corinthians 13, read “charity” as steadfast love.
words.howToRead: In 1 Corinthians 13, read “charity” as steadfast love.
words.why: When kindness feels out of reach, “charity” in the KJV points to steady, self-giving love—not how generous you look.
words.whyToday: When kindness feels out of reach, “charity” in the KJV points to steady, self-giving love—not how generous you look.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: In 1611 English, "charity" carried the sense of costly Christian love, not mainly a donation drive or fundraising appeal.
deepDive.studyNotes: Paul uses this word for the kind of love that stays when gifts, noise, and pride fall away. Read it as self-giving love that keeps choosing the good of another person.

words.note: Usually manner of life or citizenship, not small talk.
words.shortGloss: Usually manner of life or citizenship, not small talk.
words.step: Ask: “How is my walk?” when you see “conversation.”
words.howToRead: Ask: “How is my walk?” when you see “conversation.”
words.why: On days you feel scattered, remember “conversation” is often your whole walk with God, not your chat skills.
words.whyToday: On days you feel scattered, remember “conversation” is often your whole walk with God, not your chat skills.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: Older English often used "conversation" for a whole manner of life, conduct, or citizenship, not only spoken words.
deepDive.studyNotes: When Paul speaks about your conversation, he is asking how your whole walk carries the gospel. This word turns attention from polished speech to lived faithfulness.

words.note: Often “living” or “alive,” not fast.
words.shortGloss: Often “living” or “alive,” not fast.
words.step: Pair “quick” with “dead” in context to see alive vs lifeless.
words.howToRead: Pair “quick” with “dead” in context to see alive vs lifeless.
words.why: If “the quick and the dead” confuses you, you are in good company: here “quick” means alive—God’s word speaks to living hearts.
words.whyToday: If “the quick and the dead” confuses you, you are in good company: here “quick” means alive—God’s word speaks to living hearts.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The older sense of "quick" often meant living, alive, or life-giving. That is why the KJV can speak of "the quick and the dead."
deepDive.studyNotes: This word matters because it keeps you from hearing speed where the verse is teaching life. In Hebrews 4:12, the word of God is living and active, not merely fast-moving.

words.note: Treasured possession or special people set apart, not “weird.”
words.shortGloss: Treasured possession or special people set apart, not “weird.”
words.step: Hear “treasured” when you read peculiar in Titus 2:14.
words.howToRead: Hear “treasured” when you read peculiar in Titus 2:14.
words.why: When you feel overlooked, the KJV “peculiar” people are treasures set apart—seen by God.
words.whyToday: When you feel overlooked, the KJV “peculiar” people are treasures set apart—seen by God.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: In KJV-era English, "peculiar" could mean specially owned, treasured, or set apart, not merely odd or socially awkward.
deepDive.studyNotes: The point is belonging. God is not calling His people strange for strangeness' sake, but naming them as His treasured possession.

words.note: Holy Ghost is the Holy Spirit — older English for the same Person.
words.shortGloss: Holy Ghost is the Holy Spirit — older English for the same Person.
words.step: Do not read “ghost” as a spooky figure; same Comforter Jesus promised.
words.howToRead: Do not read “ghost” as a spooky figure; same Comforter Jesus promised.
words.why: If the old word unsettles you, “Holy Ghost” is the same Comforter—the Spirit Jesus promised.
words.whyToday: If the old word unsettles you, “Holy Ghost” is the same Comforter—the Spirit Jesus promised.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The English word "ghost" still served as a standard way to speak of spirit in 1611, especially in the settled phrase "Holy Ghost."
deepDive.studyNotes: Do not import modern spooky associations into this word. The KJV is speaking of the same Holy Spirit promised by Christ, present to comfort, teach, and empower.

words.note: Often “go before,” “meet,” or “come first,” not “stop.”
words.shortGloss: Often “go before,” “meet,” or “come first,” not “stop.”
words.step: In 1 Thessalonians 4:15, think “precede,” not “block.”
words.howToRead: In 1 Thessalonians 4:15, think “precede,” not “block.”
words.why: When plans feel stuck, “prevent” in older English often meant “go before” or “meet”—God still goes ahead of you.
words.whyToday: When plans feel stuck, “prevent” in older English often meant “go before” or “meet”—God still goes ahead of you.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: Older English used "prevent" for going before, anticipating, or meeting someone first, not only for stopping them.
deepDive.studyNotes: This keeps resurrection passages from sounding backward. The point is order, not obstruction: those alive will not go before the saints already asleep in Christ.

words.note: Sometimes “allow” or “let,” not only “endure pain.”
words.shortGloss: Sometimes “allow” or “let,” not only “endure pain.”
words.step: When children are named, “suffer” usually means “let them come.”
words.howToRead: When children are named, “suffer” usually means “let them come.”
words.why: When you read “suffer the little children,” hear gentle permission: let them come—not only pain language.
words.whyToday: When you read “suffer the little children,” hear gentle permission: let them come—not only pain language.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The verb "suffer" could mean permit, allow, or leave room for, alongside its pain-bearing sense.
deepDive.studyNotes: Context decides whether the word means endure pain or allow access. In Jesus' words about children, it is a tender command to stop blocking the way.

words.note: Strength, power, or moral excellence going out from Christ — not only modesty.
words.shortGloss: Strength, power, or moral excellence going out from Christ — not only modesty.
words.step: In Luke 8:46, virtue is power that went out of Him.
words.howToRead: In Luke 8:46, virtue is power that went out of Him.
words.why: When you feel drained, “virtue” in the Gospels can mean power that went out from Christ—His strength, not yours alone.
words.whyToday: When you feel drained, “virtue” in the Gospels can mean power that went out from Christ—His strength, not yours alone.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word could speak of moral excellence, but in Gospel scenes it can also carry the sense of strength or power proceeding from Christ.
deepDive.studyNotes: This helps you hear both character and power. In Luke 8, virtue is not modesty language, but power going out from Jesus to heal.

words.note: Often solid food (teaching you chew on), not only animal flesh.
words.shortGloss: Often solid food (teaching you chew on), not only animal flesh.
words.step: Contrast milk and meat when growth in doctrine is in view.
words.howToRead: Contrast milk and meat when growth in doctrine is in view.
words.why: Solid food for the mature — a reminder that growth comes slowly, one nourishing bite at a time.
words.whyToday: Solid food for the mature — a reminder that growth comes slowly, one nourishing bite at a time.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: In older English, "meat" could simply mean food, and in teaching passages it often points to solid nourishment rather than animal flesh alone.
deepDive.studyNotes: Scripture uses food imagery to describe growth. Milk is beginner nourishment; meat is teaching that requires practice, patience, and spiritual maturity.

words.note: Grain (wheat, barley), not maize.
words.shortGloss: Grain (wheat, barley), not maize.
words.step: Picture sheaves and harvest, not sweet corn on the cob.
words.howToRead: Picture sheaves and harvest, not sweet corn on the cob.
words.why: The grain that falls into the ground and dies — a picture of how new life often comes through surrender and waiting.
words.whyToday: The grain that falls into the ground and dies — a picture of how new life often comes through surrender and waiting.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The KJV uses "corn" for grain crops such as wheat or barley, not for modern maize.
deepDive.studyNotes: Reading this as grain keeps harvest passages clear and grounded in Bible-land agriculture. It preserves the ordinary field imagery the passage expects you to picture.

words.note: Fill or populate the earth, not “refill an empty tank” only.
words.shortGloss: Fill or populate the earth, not “refill an empty tank” only.
words.step: In Genesis 1:28, God fills the earth with people and life.
words.howToRead: In Genesis 1:28, God fills the earth with people and life.
words.why: When life feels empty, replenish in Genesis is about filling and fruitfulness under God’s blessing.
words.whyToday: When life feels empty, replenish in Genesis is about filling and fruitfulness under God’s blessing.

words.note: Sometimes “overcome” or “take hold of,” not only “understand.”
words.shortGloss: Sometimes “overcome” or “take hold of,” not only “understand.”
words.step: John 1:5: darkness did not overcome the light.
words.howToRead: John 1:5: darkness did not overcome the light.
words.why: When darkness feels winning, John reminds you light is not overcome—truth still stands.
words.whyToday: When darkness feels winning, John reminds you light is not overcome—truth still stands.

words.note: Private inner room for prayer, not a clothes closet only.
words.shortGloss: Private inner room for prayer, not a clothes closet only.
words.step: Picture a shut door and secret speech to the Father.
words.howToRead: Picture a shut door and secret speech to the Father.
words.why: When prayer feels exposed, Jesus points to a shut door—quiet honesty with the Father.
words.whyToday: When prayer feels exposed, Jesus points to a shut door—quiet honesty with the Father.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: A "closet" was an inner private room, chamber, or shut place, not mainly a wardrobe.
deepDive.studyNotes: Jesus is describing private prayer away from display. The force of the word is secrecy and nearness with the Father, not impressive setup.

words.note: Deep affection or compassion — idiom for the seat of feeling.
words.shortGloss: Deep affection or compassion — idiom for the seat of feeling.
words.step: Read as “tender compassion,” not anatomy lessons.
words.howToRead: Read as “tender compassion,” not anatomy lessons.
words.why: When compassion feels cold, “bowels” is old idiom for deep tenderness—God-shaped affection, not anatomy.
words.whyToday: When compassion feels cold, “bowels” is old idiom for deep tenderness—God-shaped affection, not anatomy.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: This was a common biblical-English way to speak about the deep inward seat of compassion, affection, and mercy.
deepDive.studyNotes: The word sounds clinical to modern ears, but the Bible is aiming at deep feeling. Read it as tenderhearted compassion that moves from inside outward.

words.note: Often “full of care” or anxious, not merely “attentive.”
words.shortGloss: Often “full of care” or anxious, not merely “attentive.”
words.step: Philippians 4:6 pairs “careful for nothing” with prayer.
words.howToRead: Philippians 4:6 pairs “careful for nothing” with prayer.
words.why: When worry runs the day, Philippians’ “careful for nothing” is an invitation to carry it to God in prayer.
words.whyToday: When worry runs the day, Philippians’ “careful for nothing” is an invitation to carry it to God in prayer.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: In the KJV, "careful" can mean full of care, burdened, or anxious, not simply attentive and responsible.
deepDive.studyNotes: This matters because "Be careful for nothing" is not telling you to be sloppy. It is telling anxious hearts to trade worry for prayer, thanksgiving, and trust.

words.note: Often “share” or give materially, not only “talk.”
words.shortGloss: Often “share” or give materially, not only “talk.”
words.step: Hebrews 13:16 ties sharing with doing good.
words.howToRead: Hebrews 13:16 ties sharing with doing good.
words.why: To communicate in Scripture often means to share generously — a call to open hands and open hearts.
words.whyToday: To communicate in Scripture often means to share generously — a call to open hands and open hearts.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: Older English used "communicate" for sharing goods, giving help, or entering fellowship, not only for speaking words.
deepDive.studyNotes: This word often moves from speech to generosity. The Bible is teaching shared life, where truth and tangible care belong together.

words.note: Body, human nature, kinship, or weakness — context decides.
words.shortGloss: Body, human nature, kinship, or weakness — context decides.
words.step: Track whether “flesh” means body, self, or unredeemed appetite.
words.howToRead: Track whether “flesh” means body, self, or unredeemed appetite.
words.why: When temptation is loud, “flesh” is not only your body—it can mean self-led desire that needs the Spirit’s lead.
words.whyToday: When temptation is loud, “flesh” is not only your body—it can mean self-led desire that needs the Spirit’s lead.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word can refer to the body, human weakness, family relations, or fallen self-orientation. Older readers expected context to settle the sense.
deepDive.studyNotes: This is one of the most important context words in the KJV. Sometimes it is simple embodiment; sometimes it is self-directed life resisting the Spirit.

words.note: Sheol, grave, or Gehenna by context — not one English place every time.
words.shortGloss: Sheol, grave, or Gehenna by context — not one English place every time.
words.step: Let surrounding verses show whether grave, judgment, or imagery.
words.howToRead: Let surrounding verses show whether grave, judgment, or imagery.
words.why: When the word frightens you, let each verse show whether grave, judgment, or imagery—read with context, not panic.
words.whyToday: When the word frightens you, let each verse show whether grave, judgment, or imagery—read with context, not panic.

words.note: Will, mind, and inner person — not only emotion.
words.shortGloss: Will, mind, and inner person — not only emotion.
words.step: “As he thinketh in his heart” is orientation, not only mood.
words.howToRead: “As he thinketh in his heart” is orientation, not only mood.
words.why: When emotions swing, “heart” in scripture is your inner direction—what you treasure and choose—not only feelings.
words.whyToday: When emotions swing, “heart” in scripture is your inner direction—what you treasure and choose—not only feelings.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: Biblical "heart" names the inner person: mind, will, desire, and moral direction, not just a passing emotional state.
deepDive.studyNotes: Scripture treats the heart as the command center of a life. That is why guarding it matters: what rules the heart eventually shapes words, habits, and worship.

words.note: Life, self, appetite, or person — overlaps with heart and spirit.
words.shortGloss: Life, self, appetite, or person — overlaps with heart and spirit.
words.step: Ask whether the verse means life, inner life, or appetite.
words.howToRead: Ask whether the verse means life, inner life, or appetite.
words.why: When you feel undone, “soul” often means your life before God—breath, appetite, self—He cares for the whole person.
words.whyToday: When you feel undone, “soul” often means your life before God—breath, appetite, self—He cares for the whole person.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The KJV uses "soul" flexibly for life itself, the self, the person, or the inward life before God.
deepDive.studyNotes: The word is bigger than a neat body-soul chart. Often it names the whole living person in relation to God, hunger, danger, hope, or rest.

words.note: Breath, attitude, unclean spirit, or Holy Spirit — let the verse choose.
words.shortGloss: Breath, attitude, unclean spirit, or Holy Spirit — let the verse choose.
words.step: Capitalization in print helps; in audio, context must.
words.howToRead: Capitalization in print helps; in audio, context must.
words.why: When you are spiritually tired, “spirit” might mean breath, attitude, evil spirit, or Holy Spirit—let the verse decide.
words.whyToday: When you are spiritually tired, “spirit” might mean breath, attitude, evil spirit, or Holy Spirit—let the verse decide.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word can mean breath, inner disposition, evil spirit, or the Holy Spirit. KJV readers were expected to let context do the work.
deepDive.studyNotes: This is a careful-reading word. Ask whether the verse is speaking about God's Spirit, a human spirit, a spiritual atmosphere, or a creaturely spirit.

words.note: Change of mind that shows in turning — not mere regret.
words.shortGloss: Change of mind that shows in turning — not mere regret.
words.step: Look for fruit that matches the turning.
words.howToRead: Look for fruit that matches the turning.
words.why: When shame is loud, repentance is turning toward mercy—not wallowing.
words.whyToday: When shame is loud, repentance is turning toward mercy—not wallowing.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The biblical sense reaches beyond regret into a change of mind and direction that shows itself in real turning.
deepDive.studyNotes: Repentance is not self-loathing for its own sake. It is Godward turning that agrees with the truth and walks toward mercy.

words.note: Declared righteous before God by faith — not “earned by behavior first.”
words.shortGloss: Declared righteous before God by faith — not “earned by behavior first.”
words.step: Distinguish standing before God from growth in holiness.
words.howToRead: Distinguish standing before God from growth in holiness.
words.why: When your mind replays failure, justification is God’s righteous verdict on everyone who trusts Christ.
words.whyToday: When your mind replays failure, justification is God’s righteous verdict on everyone who trusts Christ.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: This is courtroom language: to justify is to declare righteous or vindicated, not first to make morally perfect.
deepDive.studyNotes: You hear the gospel more clearly when this stays legal and relational. God justifies the ungodly by faith in Christ, then begins the lifelong work of renewal.

words.note: Set apart for God; status and growth both appear.
words.shortGloss: Set apart for God; status and growth both appear.
words.step: Note past tense “were sanctified” and ongoing “be holy.”
words.howToRead: Note past tense “were sanctified” and ongoing “be holy.”
words.why: When growth feels slow, sanctification is both God’s gift and daily becoming more His.
words.whyToday: When growth feels slow, sanctification is both God’s gift and daily becoming more His.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word can speak both of being set apart for God and of the ongoing process of holiness in life.
deepDive.studyNotes: The KJV lets both senses stand together. Believers are sanctified in Christ, and believers are still being sanctified in the shape of daily obedience.

words.note: Wrath absorbed; mercy-seat reality — God’s justice and love meet.
words.shortGloss: Wrath absorbed; mercy-seat reality — God’s justice and love meet.
words.step: Think “satisfied justice,” not a cold word only.
words.howToRead: Think “satisfied justice,” not a cold word only.
words.why: When guilt feels unbearable, this word quietly says God’s justice and love met in Christ—for you.
words.whyToday: When guilt feels unbearable, this word quietly says God’s justice and love met in Christ—for you.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: This church word carried the sense of wrath answered, justice satisfied, and mercy-seat fulfillment in Christ.
deepDive.studyNotes: Do not flatten this into a cold formula. The word shows that at the cross God did not ignore sin; He dealt with it fully so mercy could be righteous and real.

words.note: Counted to your account — Abraham’s faith reckoned as righteousness (idea in Romans 4).
words.shortGloss: Counted to your account — Abraham’s faith reckoned as righteousness (idea in Romans 4).
words.step: Follow “reckon” and “impute” in Romans 4 in one sitting.
words.howToRead: Follow “reckon” and “impute” in Romans 4 in one sitting.
words.why: When guilt says “not enough,” imputation is God counting faith to you for righteousness—His gift, not your résumé.
words.whyToday: When guilt says “not enough,” imputation is God counting faith to you for righteousness—His gift, not your résumé.

words.note: Binding promise God makes and keeps; new covenant in Christ’s blood.
words.shortGloss: Binding promise God makes and keeps; new covenant in Christ’s blood.
words.step: Old and new contrast in Hebrews is about better promises.
words.howToRead: Old and new contrast in Hebrews is about better promises.
words.why: When promises feel fragile, covenant is God binding Himself—faithful when we are not.
words.whyToday: When promises feel fragile, covenant is God binding Himself—faithful when we are not.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: A covenant is a binding pledge or administered promise, especially in God's dealings with His people.
deepDive.studyNotes: The Bible does not present salvation as vague good intentions. Covenant language shows God binding Himself by promise, climaxing in the new covenant sealed by Christ's blood.

words.note: Tent of meeting; God dwelling with a moving people; shadow of Christ.
words.shortGloss: Tent of meeting; God dwelling with a moving people; shadow of Christ.
words.step: John 1:14: “dwelt” is tabernacled among us.
words.howToRead: John 1:14: “dwelt” is tabernacled among us.
words.why: When church feels distant, remember God tabernacled among us—He draws near to sinners in Christ.
words.whyToday: When church feels distant, remember God tabernacled among us—He draws near to sinners in Christ.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word names the portable tent of meeting, but it also became rich symbolic language for God dwelling with His people.
deepDive.studyNotes: This word is a thread of presence. From the wilderness tent to Christ dwelling among us to the final dwelling of God with man, it teaches nearness without loss of holiness.

words.note: Covering of sin; fulfilled in the one final sacrifice.
words.shortGloss: Covering of sin; fulfilled in the one final sacrifice.
words.step: Hebrews shows one offering versus repeated shadows.
words.howToRead: Hebrews shows one offering versus repeated shadows.
words.why: When sin feels sticky, atonement is sin covered and answered—pointing to one final sacrifice.
words.whyToday: When sin feels sticky, atonement is sin covered and answered—pointing to one final sacrifice.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The KJV word speaks of sin being covered, answered, and reconciled through sacrifice under God's appointed way.
deepDive.studyNotes: The old covenant sacrifices prepared the mind to understand Christ. Hebrews makes clear that all those coverings point forward to the one final offering that truly cleanses.

words.note: Bought back — a price paid, ownership changed.
words.shortGloss: Bought back — a price paid, ownership changed.
words.step: Tie redemption to ransom language without sensationalism.
words.howToRead: Tie redemption to ransom language without sensationalism.
words.why: When life feels owned by fear or habit, redemption is being bought back—belonging to the Lord again.
words.whyToday: When life feels owned by fear or habit, redemption is being bought back—belonging to the Lord again.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word belongs to the language of ransom, release, and bought-back freedom.
deepDive.studyNotes: Redemption answers the question of ownership. Christ does not merely improve you; He purchases you out of bondage and claims you for Himself.

words.note: God’s favor you did not earn — not permission to sin.
words.shortGloss: God’s favor you did not earn — not permission to sin.
words.step: Pair Ephesians 2:8–9 with Romans 6 on new life.
words.howToRead: Pair Ephesians 2:8–9 with Romans 6 on new life.
words.why: On days you feel you have to earn rest, grace is God’s favor meeting you before you proved anything.
words.whyToday: On days you feel you have to earn rest, grace is God’s favor meeting you before you proved anything.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: Grace names undeserved favor, but also the active kindness of God that saves, strengthens, teaches, and keeps.
deepDive.studyNotes: Grace is more than a doorway word. It is the atmosphere of Christian life from start to finish: pardon for the guilty and strength for the weak.

words.note: Trust resting on God’s word; shows in obedience.
words.shortGloss: Trust resting on God’s word; shows in obedience.
words.step: Faith and works tensions resolve when faith is living.
words.howToRead: Faith and works tensions resolve when faith is living.
words.why: When you cannot see the next step, faith is trust anchored in what God has said.
words.whyToday: When you cannot see the next step, faith is trust anchored in what God has said.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: Biblical faith means trust, reliance, and fidelity rooted in God's word, not a vague positive outlook.
deepDive.studyNotes: Faith receives what grace gives. It does not compete with obedience; living faith leans on God so deeply that obedience begins to grow from the inside out.

words.note: Deeds — not ground of salvation, yet faith without deeds is dead.
words.shortGloss: Deeds — not ground of salvation, yet faith without deeds is dead.
words.step: Ephesians 2:8–10 holds both grace and workmanship together.
words.howToRead: Ephesians 2:8–10 holds both grace and workmanship together.
words.why: When you fear you are never doing enough, scripture still says true faith shows up in real love and obedience.
words.whyToday: When you fear you are never doing enough, scripture still says true faith shows up in real love and obedience.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word speaks of deeds, acts, and labor. In salvation discussions it must be handled carefully with Paul and James both open.
deepDive.studyNotes: Works do not earn union with Christ, yet true faith is never barren. Scripture refuses both prideful earning and empty profession.

words.note: Age, order, or people on earth — context narrows meaning.
words.shortGloss: Age, order, or people on earth — context narrows meaning.
words.step: Ask: moral system, planet, or people?
words.howToRead: Ask: moral system, planet, or people?
words.why: When headlines overwhelm, “world” can mean creation, age, or value-system—ask which one the verse targets.
words.whyToday: When headlines overwhelm, “world” can mean creation, age, or value-system—ask which one the verse targets.

words.note: Assembly — local gathered body and Christ’s people overall.
words.shortGloss: Assembly — local gathered body and Christ’s people overall.
words.step: Building metaphor is people, not brick idolatry.
words.howToRead: Building metaphor is people, not brick idolatry.
words.why: When fellowship hurts, “church” is the called-out assembly—people under Christ’s headship, still being sanctified.
words.whyToday: When fellowship hurts, “church” is the called-out assembly—people under Christ’s headship, still being sanctified.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The basic sense is assembly or called-out gathering, whether local congregation or the people of Christ more broadly.
deepDive.studyNotes: This word protects against reducing church to a building or brand. The church is Christ's gathered people, loved by Him and formed under His word.

words.note: Overseer — pastoral office of care and sound teaching.
words.shortGloss: Overseer — pastoral office of care and sound teaching.
words.step: Often overlaps elder; watch context for office vs gift.
words.howToRead: Often overlaps elder; watch context for office vs gift.
words.why: When leadership disappoints, bishop is overseer language—gifted care, answerable to the Chief Shepherd.
words.whyToday: When leadership disappoints, bishop is overseer language—gifted care, answerable to the Chief Shepherd.

words.note: Demons, unclean spirits — Christ’s authority is absolute.
words.shortGloss: Demons, unclean spirits — Christ’s authority is absolute.
words.step: No fascination — flee to Christ’s word and presence.
words.howToRead: No fascination — flee to Christ’s word and presence.
words.why: Even when darkness feels close, these words remind us that God's light has already overcome it.
words.whyToday: Even when darkness feels close, these words remind us that God's light has already overcome it.

words.note: Fermented drink in many uses; wisdom warns excess.
words.shortGloss: Fermented drink in many uses; wisdom warns excess.
words.step: Let context show celebration, medicine, or warning.
words.howToRead: Let context show celebration, medicine, or warning.
words.why: Wine in Scripture often points to joy and celebration — a picture of the abundant life God wants to pour into our weary hearts.
words.whyToday: Wine in Scripture often points to joy and celebration — a picture of the abundant life God wants to pour into our weary hearts.

words.note: Judgment image — treading out God’s wrath in Scripture imagery.
words.shortGloss: Judgment image — treading out God’s wrath in Scripture imagery.
words.step: Read as sobering picture, not glee.
words.howToRead: Read as sobering picture, not glee.
words.why: When judgment language sounds violent, the winepress is sober harvest imagery—God’s justice is real; let it move you toward Christ, not toward glee.
words.whyToday: When judgment language sounds violent, the winepress is sober harvest imagery—God’s justice is real; let it move you toward Christ, not toward glee.

words.note: Building, Christ’s body, or believer — track the referent.
words.shortGloss: Building, Christ’s body, or believer — track the referent.
words.step: Paul’s “your body is the temple” is personal holiness.
words.howToRead: Paul’s “your body is the temple” is personal holiness.
words.why: Your body is now the temple — a quiet reminder that God chooses to dwell with you, even on the hardest days.

deepDive.studyNotes: Halting in Elijah's challenge is more than indecision. It is divided allegiance. Scripture uses the image well because spiritual wobbling feels like limping: unstable, tiring, and hard to hide for long.

words.shortGloss: Go get, bring — plain narrative verb.
words.step: Swap “go get” mentally when fetch appears—story keeps moving.
words.howToRead: Swap “go get” mentally when fetch appears—story keeps moving.
words.why: When old verbs slow you down, fetch is simple errand-language—keep reading; the point is usually obedience, not vocabulary.
words.whyToday: When old verbs slow you down, fetch is simple errand-language—keep reading; the point is usually obedience, not vocabulary.

words.note: Suitable timing or opportunity — not merely “handy.”
words.shortGloss: Suitable timing or opportunity — not merely “handy.”
words.step: Herod’s “convenient day” is planned indulgence—watch when convenience serves sin.
words.howToRead: Herod’s “convenient day” is planned indulgence—watch when convenience serves sin.
words.why: When someone says “not convenient,” Scripture often means timing—good for honest delay, dangerous as an excuse to dodge conscience.
words.whyToday: When someone says “not convenient,” Scripture often means timing—good for honest delay, dangerous as an excuse to dodge conscience.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word can mean suitable, opportune, seasonable, or fitting to a moment, not merely handy or easy.
deepDive.studyNotes: This word often reveals the moral use of timing. Sometimes convenience serves wisdom; sometimes it becomes a shield for delay, indulgence, or cowardice. Felix is the warning case: a more convenient season never becomes repentance.

words.note: Turtledove — bird of the poets, not a reptile.
words.shortGloss: Turtledove — bird of the poets, not a reptile.
words.step: Song of Solomon 2:12 signals spring and return—creation praising with the singer.
words.howToRead: Song of Solomon 2:12 signals spring and return—creation praising with the singer.
words.why: When “turtle” confuses modern ears, think turtledove—Scripture is hearing creation and seasons, not a zoo joke.
words.whyToday: When “turtle” confuses modern ears, think turtledove—Scripture is hearing creation and seasons, not a zoo joke.

words.note: Farmer, cultivator — God and patience with the field.
words.shortGloss: Farmer, cultivator — God and patience with the field.
words.step: James 5:7: the husbandman waits for fruit—so wait on the Lord’s timing.
words.howToRead: James 5:7: the husbandman waits for fruit—so wait on the Lord’s timing.
words.why: When waiting grinds you, husbandman language honors slow growth—God is patient with soil, weather, and souls.
words.whyToday: When waiting grinds you, husbandman language honors slow growth—God is patient with soil, weather, and souls.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: A husbandman is a cultivator or farmer, especially one who patiently works land for harvest.
deepDive.studyNotes: This word is slow-growth wisdom. The husbandman does not yank fruit out of the ground. He waits, tends, and trusts the season. Scripture uses that patience to teach believers how God works in fields and hearts alike.

words.note: Womb — where life begins under God’s numbering.
words.shortGloss: Womb — where life begins under God’s numbering.
words.step: Firstborn and matrix texts show life belongs to God—read reverently.
words.howToRead: Firstborn and matrix texts show life belongs to God—read reverently.
words.why: When “matrix” sounds sci-fi, the KJV means womb—life is framed as sacred, not disposable.
words.whyToday: When “matrix” sounds sci-fi, the KJV means womb—life is framed as sacred, not disposable.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: In KJV usage the matrix is the womb, especially in laws about firstborn life opening it.
deepDive.studyNotes: This is a sacred-life word, not a strange technicality. The firstborn laws remind Israel that life, birth, and belonging are under God's claim. The strangeness of the term can hide the tenderness of the truth if read too quickly.

words.note: Earnest care, godly zeal — can be grief-born attention.
words.shortGloss: Earnest care, godly zeal — can be grief-born attention.
words.step: 2 Corinthians 7:11 lists fruits of godly sorrow—carefulness is alert love.
words.howToRead: 2 Corinthians 7:11 lists fruits of godly sorrow—carefulness is alert love.
words.why: When worry masquerades as love, carefulness in Scripture is often holy attention—turn it into prayer and action, not spinning thoughts.
words.whyToday: When worry masquerades as love, carefulness in Scripture is often holy attention—turn it into prayer and action, not spinning thoughts.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word can mean earnest care, serious concern, or alert diligence, especially where godly sorrow produces real action.
deepDive.studyNotes: This is one of the places where scripture separates holy care from anxious spinning. In 2 Corinthians 7, carefulness is the awake, honest, responsible fruit of repentance, not fretfulness without movement.

words.note: Jealous rivalry, zealous contention — not modern “emulate a hero.”
words.shortGloss: Jealous rivalry, zealous contention — not modern “emulate a hero.”
words.step: Works of the flesh include emulations—compare yourself less; bless more.
words.howToRead: Works of the flesh include emulations—compare yourself less; bless more.
words.why: When you itch to prove you are ahead, emulation warns about rivalry—let humility and honor cool the heat.
words.whyToday: When you itch to prove you are ahead, emulation warns about rivalry—let humility and honor cool the heat.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: Emulation here means jealous rivalry, competitive zeal, or status-chasing contention rather than wholesome imitation.
deepDive.studyNotes: The word belongs in the works-of-the-flesh list because rivalry can wear a respectable face. Emulation turns another person's gift into a threat and quietly trains the heart to compete instead of love.

words.note: Party excess, carousing — loud indulgence.
words.shortGloss: Party excess, carousing — loud indulgence.
words.step: Peter reminds former patterns—freedom in Christ is clean joy.
words.howToRead: Peter reminds former patterns—freedom in Christ is clean joy.
words.why: When fun demands numbness, revellings name the empty kind—joy in Christ satisfies without stealing tomorrow.
words.whyToday: When fun demands numbness, revellings name the empty kind—joy in Christ satisfies without stealing tomorrow.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word refers to noisy carousing, party excess, and indulgent celebration that dulls the soul.
deepDive.studyNotes: Revellings are not simple gladness. They are joy detached from sobriety and truth. Scripture names them because the flesh likes celebration that asks nothing of conscience and costs dearly the next morning.

words.note: Strife, division — household and church fractures.
words.shortGloss: Strife, division — household and church fractures.
words.step: Jesus names gospel cost—truth can split what false peace held together.
words.howToRead: Jesus names gospel cost—truth can split what false peace held together.
words.why: When faith costs relationships, variance is honest friction—love still; cleave to Christ first.
words.whyToday: When faith costs relationships, variance is honest friction—love still; cleave to Christ first.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: Variance means strife, discord, or standing at odds with one another, especially where relationships fracture under pride or truth-pressure.
deepDive.studyNotes: Not all conflict is the same. Some variance comes from the gospel dividing false peace, and some comes from fleshly rivalry. The word is useful because it forces the reader to ask what kind of division is present.

words.note: Large unit of money in parables — capacity entrusted, not only “skill.”
words.shortGloss: Large unit of money in parables — capacity entrusted, not only “skill.”
words.step: Parable talents test faithfulness—small or great, invest what God gave.
words.howToRead: Parable talents test faithfulness—small or great, invest what God gave.
words.why: When you feel “untalented,” the parable is about trust with whatever measure you hold—faithful beats flashy.
words.whyToday: When you feel “untalented,” the parable is about trust with whatever measure you hold—faithful beats flashy.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: A talent is a large measure of money or weight in scripture, especially in parables where entrusted value becomes a test of faithfulness.
deepDive.studyNotes: Modern talk can reduce this to personal gifting, but Jesus' parable keeps the weight on stewardship. What has been entrusted must not be buried in fear. The issue is faithful handling under the Master's return.

words.note: Small coin — worth varies by story; God counts little things.
words.shortGloss: Small coin — worth varies by story; God counts little things.
words.step: Two sparrows for a farthing logic—pennies prove divine attention.
words.howToRead: Two sparrows for a farthing logic—pennies prove divine attention.
words.why: When you feel unseen, penny texts argue the opposite—God’s math includes what the world calls pocket change.
words.whyToday: When you feel unseen, penny texts argue the opposite—God’s math includes what the world calls pocket change.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The penny in the KJV often represents a small coin or wage unit in stories about value, labor, and attention.
deepDive.studyNotes: Penny passages matter because scripture keeps exposing heaven's different math. The coin may look small, but it becomes a lens for God's generosity, human envy, and His notice of what others ignore.

words.note: Outer garment — justice, travel, and generosity scenes.
words.shortGloss: Outer garment — justice, travel, and generosity scenes.
words.step: Matthew 5:40 is radical generosity—read as Jesus’ kingdom ethic, not coercion.
words.howToRead: Matthew 5:40 is radical generosity—read as Jesus’ kingdom ethic, not coercion.
words.why: When rights tighten your fist, cloak passages test love—generosity flows from security in God, not from being walked over with bitterness.
words.whyToday: When rights tighten your fist, cloak passages test love—generosity flows from security in God, not from being walked over with bitterness.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word names an outer garment, often bound up with covering, travel, mercy, justice, and sacrificial generosity.
deepDive.studyNotes: Cloak is not a random wardrobe detail in scripture. In law and teaching it becomes a test of how you treat vulnerability, rights, and neighbor-love. Jesus uses it to stretch the heart beyond strict self-protection.

words.note: Cloth — face wrapping, burial detail, stewardship parable.
words.shortGloss: Cloth — face wrapping, burial detail, stewardship parable.
words.step: John 20:7: folded napkin signals orderly resurrection hope.
words.howToRead: John 20:7: folded napkin signals orderly resurrection hope.
words.why: When a napkin shows up in Scripture, slow down—God is in tender details, from graves to coins wrapped in cloth.
words.whyToday: When a napkin shows up in Scripture, slow down—God is in tender details, from graves to coins wrapped in cloth.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: A napkin is a cloth or wrapping, whether around a face, around money, or laid aside in burial scenes.
deepDive.studyNotes: Napkin passages are small-detail passages, but scripture often stores meaning there. In John 20 the ordered cloth quietly witnesses to a risen Lord who was not stolen in panic. In Luke 19 the wrapped coin exposes fearful stewardship.

words.note: Tax collector — often a humbled heart versus proud religion.
words.shortGloss: Tax collector — often a humbled heart versus proud religion.
words.step: The publican’s prayer beats the Pharisee’s posture—mercy over performance.
words.howToRead: The publican’s prayer beats the Pharisee’s posture—mercy over performance.
words.why: When “publican” sounds like insult, Jesus often sets them as models of repentance—honest need meets honest grace.
words.whyToday: When “publican” sounds like insult, Jesus often sets them as models of repentance—honest need meets honest grace.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word names a tax collector, a figure often despised in Jewish society because of compromise, greed, and Roman association.
deepDive.studyNotes: Publican becomes an important gospel word because Jesus keeps placing mercy beside religious pride. The publican in Luke 18 brings no polished record, only an honest plea, and he goes down justified.

words.note: Healer — Christ’s mission and human humility.
words.shortGloss: Healer — Christ’s mission and human humility.
words.step: “Physician, heal thyself” can be proverb or sarcasm—watch tone.
words.howToRead: “Physician, heal thyself” can be proverb or sarcasm—watch tone.
words.why: When you pretend you are fine, physician texts invite honesty—Christ came for the sick, not for polished masks.
words.whyToday: When you pretend you are fine, physician texts invite honesty—Christ came for the sick, not for polished masks.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: A physician is a healer or doctor, and Jesus uses the image proverbially for the purpose of His own ministry.
deepDive.studyNotes: The force of the word is not admiration of medicine alone. Christ is exposing denial. Healthy people do not seek a physician; the sick do. The gospel begins where need is admitted instead of hidden.

words.note: Narrow, tight, strict — gate, way, discipline.
words.shortGloss: Narrow, tight, strict — gate, way, discipline.
words.step: Strait gate is not meanness—life is found in the narrow way of Christ.
words.howToRead: Strait gate is not meanness—life is found in the narrow way of Christ.
words.why: When “strait” feels like squeeze, it is tight-shoe faith—real life often starts where the crowd thins and Christ is clear.
words.whyToday: When “strait” feels like squeeze, it is tight-shoe faith—real life often starts where the crowd thins and Christ is clear.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The older word means narrow, tight, compressed, or difficult, especially in the image of the narrow gate and constricted way.
deepDive.studyNotes: Strait does not mean cruel. Jesus is teaching that life is not found in roomy self-rule but in the narrow way that passes through repentance, faith, and obedience. The squeeze is real, but it leads somewhere living.

words.note: Steady, fixed, settled — older spelling of steadfast.
words.shortGloss: Steady, fixed, settled — older spelling of steadfast.
words.step: Read stedfast as anchored faithfulness, not rigid pride.
words.howToRead: Read stedfast as anchored faithfulness, not rigid pride.
words.why: When everything shifts, stedfast is the gospel word for settled endurance — rooted, watchful, and not easily moved.
words.whyToday: When everything shifts, stedfast is the gospel word for settled endurance — rooted, watchful, and not easily moved.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: This older spelling means steadfast: fixed, settled, anchored, and not easily turned aside.
deepDive.studyNotes: Stedfast is quiet endurance, not stiff pride. It is the kind of constancy that keeps praying, obeying, and standing when a season tries to shake you loose.

words.note: Earnest asking — humble pleading prayer before God.
words.shortGloss: Earnest asking — humble pleading prayer before God.
words.step: Supplication is lowly, specific prayer — not polished speech.
words.howToRead: Supplication is lowly, specific prayer — not polished speech.
words.why: When you do not have fancy words, supplication reminds you that needy prayer is welcome prayer.
words.whyToday: When you do not have fancy words, supplication reminds you that needy prayer is welcome prayer.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: Supplication speaks of earnest pleading, humble asking, and prayer that knows its need before God.
deepDive.studyNotes: This word keeps prayer low to the ground. Supplication is not performance for heaven. It is needy prayer, often specific and repeated, brought before a Father who invites you to ask.

words.note: Self-control — desires governed under grace.
words.shortGloss: Self-control — desires governed under grace.
words.step: Temperance is not cold repression; it is Spirit-shaped restraint.
words.howToRead: Temperance is not cold repression; it is Spirit-shaped restraint.
words.why: When appetite feels louder than wisdom, temperance is grace teaching the body and mind to live under Christ’s rule.
words.whyToday: When appetite feels louder than wisdom, temperance is grace teaching the body and mind to live under Christ’s rule.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word means self-control, mastery, or disciplined restraint rather than personality chill or emotional shutdown.
deepDive.studyNotes: Temperance is not coldness. It is desire brought under a better King. The Bible treats it as fruit of the Spirit and as a grace to be pursued with diligence.

words.note: Troubled, tormented, or worn down — inwardly or outwardly pressed.
words.shortGloss: Troubled, tormented, or worn down — inwardly or outwardly pressed.
words.step: Let vexed name real torment without letting torment define the whole story.
words.howToRead: Let vexed name real torment without letting torment define the whole story.
words.why: When a passage sounds intense, vexed gives honest language for being deeply troubled — and leaves room for Christ to bring relief.
words.whyToday: When a passage sounds intense, vexed gives honest language for being deeply troubled — and leaves room for Christ to bring relief.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word can mean harassed, tormented, troubled, or worn down, whether by oppression, sin around you, or spiritual affliction.
deepDive.studyNotes: Vexed is strong language for real trouble. Scripture uses it when souls are pressed, not mildly annoyed. That honesty matters because Christ meets people in true torment, not in cleaned-up summaries.

words.note: Stay awake, keep guard, stay spiritually alert — especially in prayer.
words.shortGloss: Stay awake, keep guard, stay spiritually alert — especially in prayer.
words.step: Watch is active readiness, not nervous panic.
words.howToRead: Watch is active readiness, not nervous panic.
words.why: When life goes numb, watch is a gentle wake-up word — stay near, stay praying, stay awake to what matters.
words.whyToday: When life goes numb, watch is a gentle wake-up word — stay near, stay praying, stay awake to what matters.

deepDive.kjvEraUsage: The word joins wakefulness, guarding, and alert waiting. In Jesus' teaching it often leans toward prayerful readiness.
deepDive.studyNotes: Watch is not a command to become paranoid. It is a call to stay awake to temptation, to time, and to the Lord's presence. The Bible pairs watchfulness with prayer because sleepy hearts drift fast.
